issues.failure_explanation: Testing the two update equations with theta^{-1} rho^n v^{n+theta} and (alpha*theta)^{-1} varphi^{n+theta} and applying the polarization identity quoted in the proofs yields the dissipation (theta-1/2)*{ int rho^n |v^{n+1}-v^n|^2 + (1/alpha)||grad varphi^{n+1}-grad varphi^n||^2 } (lumped analogues in the fully discrete case) - exactly twice the stated bracket (theta-1/2)*(1/2alpha)*int{alpha*rho_n|dv|^2+|d(grad varphi)|^2}. Exact evaluation of the scheme confirms this: in the constant-coefficient model v^{n+theta}+i*theta*tau*w^{n+theta}=v^n, w^{n+theta}+i*theta*tau*v^{n+theta}=w^n with theta=1, v^n=1, w^n=0, one gets E^{n+1}=1/4 and an increment contribution of 1/4, so E^n=E^{n+1}+1/4, whereas the stated identity would require E^{n+1}+1/8=E^n. Both stated identities are therefore false for theta != 1/2 (they hold only at theta=1/2 where the term vanishes); the correct prefactor is 2*theta-1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the prefactor (theta-1/2) by (2*theta-1) (equivalently, double the dissipation bracket) in Lemma lem:semi_discrete_parabolic_energy_balance and in Proposition prop:fully_discrete_parabolic_energy_balance.

issues.failure_explanation: The bilinear form consists solely of gradient terms, so a_{n,theta}(c,c)=0 for every constant c != 0 while ||c||_{H^1(D)} > 0: it is not coercive on H^1(D) (only modulo constants, or on H^1_0 under Dirichlet data, neither of which is assumed). The gradient-level bound a(varphi,varphi) >= ||grad varphi||^2 additionally requires rho^n >= 0, but only rho^n in L^infinity is supposed. Moreover the boundedness constant is 1 + O(tau_n^2*omega_p^2) (it is at least 1 because of the Laplacian term, as in Proposition prop:boundedness), not O(tau_n^2*omega_p^2). Consequently the well-posedness asserted in Corollary cor:added-1 - where the discrete problem, stated without boundary conditions, determines varphi_h^{n+theta} only up to constants - is not established.

issues.failure_explanation: By the reconstruction, the mechanical part of the stated sums equals (internal part) + (1/2)*KE, where KE = sum (1/2) m rho^n |v|^2 is exactly the kinetic term of Proposition prop:fully_discrete_parabolic_energy_balance, while the potential part PE = (1/2alpha)||grad varphi||^2 enters unscaled. The proposition gives KE^{n+1} + PE^{n+1} + (theta-1/2)(...) = KE^n + PE^n, which implies the inequality only for sum m*E (without the 1/2), not for the stated half-weighted mechanical energy. Indeed, at theta=1/2 the stated left-minus-right difference equals (1/2)(KE^n - KE^{n+1}), which is positive whenever kinetic energy is converted into potential energy: e.g. in the constant-coefficient model of the theta scheme (theta=1/2, v^n=1, w^n=0) kinetic energy drops from 1/2 to 0.18 while potential energy rises from 0 to 0.32, so the stated left side (0.09+0.32=0.41) exceeds the stated right side (0.25). Both the claimed inequality and the claimed equality at theta=1/2 fail; the internal-energy parts cancel and do not affect the violation.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof does not establish the stated residual bounds. (i) The auxiliary equation presented as a theta-discretization of the mass balance carries a wrong sign and a spurious factor alpha: testing partial_t rho + div(rho v) = 0 gives <rho-tilde, omega>_h - theta*tau <rho-tilde*v-breve, grad omega> = <rho^n, omega>_h, so the displayed +theta*tau*alpha version does not reproduce the residual difference alpha*<rho^{n+theta} - rho-tilde^{n+theta}, omega>_h that the argument requires. (ii) The central consistency estimate ||rho-tilde^{n+theta} - rho^{n+theta}|| = O(tau_n^2) is merely assumed; the proof itself states it would need to be verified in detail for the concrete chosen method. (iii) The lumped-versus-L^2 product error O(tau_n*h^s) and (iv) the improved O(h^3 + h^{1+s}) rate for theta=1/2 are asserted without any argument. Neither stated rate is established.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose asserts that the boundedness constant of a_h^{n,theta} scales like O(tau_n*omega_p^2). The coupling coefficient of the bilinear form is theta^2*tau_n^2*alpha (with omega_p^2 = alpha*rho), and the very proposition cited in the same sentence establishes the constant 1 + c*tau_n^2*alpha*||rho_h^n||_{h,infinity} = 1 + O(tau_n^2*omega_p^2) - one more power of tau_n than claimed. In the magnetic-drift regime (tau_n of order 1e-3 to 1e-4, omega_p of order 1e6) the stated scaling misrepresents the conditioning of the source-update operator by roughly three orders of magnitude.
